definition: The process of analyzing large datasets to discover patterns, trends, and relationships that can be used to make predictions or gain insights about individuals or groups.
metaDescription: Learn about data mining - how companies analyze large datasets to discover patterns and make predictions about your behavior and preferences.
simpleExplanation: Data mining is like digital detective work where companies sift through massive amounts of information to find hidden patterns. Think of it as looking through thousands of shopping receipts to figure out what products people buy together.
whyItMatters: Data mining affects your privacy because it can reveal intimate details about your life, preferences, and behavior that you never explicitly shared. Companies use these insights to target ads, set prices, or make decisions about you.
technicalDetail: Data mining employs statistical algorithms, machine learning, and pattern recognition techniques to process structured and unstructured data. Common methods include clustering, classification, association rules, and regression analysis to extract actionable intelligence from raw data.

examples.explanation: Amazon analyzes your browsing history, purchases, and similar users' behavior to recommend products you might want to buy.
Credit agencies mine your financial data, payment history, and spending patterns to predict your likelihood of repaying loans.
Facebook analyzes your posts, likes, and connections to determine your interests and show you targeted advertisements.
